thread:
Erin (CS): FYI — Acme reported weird output inconsistencies after yesterday's canary. They say the same prompt sometimes returns a short, factual summary and other times it adds hallucinated steps. :eyes:
Alex (Acme): Confirming. We sent identical payloads from our app, sometimes we get the correct list, sometimes an invented 'step 4' that is wrong. Happening across multiple requests within same conversation ID.
Erin (CS): Customer shared examples and request-ids, pasting below. They suspect it started right after the model routing change rolled yesterday (canary -> staged).
Alex (Acme): Example 1 (good): request_id=acme-req-1823
POST /v1/generate body:
```json
{"model":"redwood-7b-v1.3","input":"Summarize how to onboard a user in our app"}
```
response (good):
```
1) Create account
2) Verify email
3) Add profile details
```
Alex (Acme): Example 2 (bad): request_id=acme-req-1827
POST /v1/generate body same as above
response (bad):
```
1) Create account
2) Verify email
3) Add profile details
4) Set up OAuth with provider X (not applicable)
```
Alex (Acme): Both calls within ~2s, same conversation_id=conv-9c3, same client version.
Rafael (eng-runtime): Thanks — that sounds like a routing fallback to a different model variant. Looking at routing logs for Acme's tenant id (tenant_acme) around ts 1763001200-1763001300.
sre-bot: route-log: tenant=tenant_acme request=acme-req-1823 route=redwood-7b-v1.3 variant=fp16 fallback=false node=gpu-a1
sre-bot: route-log: tenant=tenant_acme request=acme-req-1827 route=redwood-7b-v1.3 variant=q4_0 fallback=true node=cpu-batch-7
Priya (eng-platform): Oof — fallback=true and variant=q4_0 explains numeric differences. We do soft-fallbacks when capacity is constrained or when model pre-warm isn't available. But we should not fallback to variants that change semantics for production customers without explicit config.
Rafael (eng-runtime): Repro steps for us: run this curl twice rapidly to try to hit both codepaths:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Client-Request-Id: acme-test-$$" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-v1.3","input":"Summarize how to onboard a user in our app","conversation_id":"conv-9c3"}'
```
Add `-H "X-Tenant-Id: tenant_acme"` to force tenant routing. Look at response metadata headers: `x-redwood-variant` and `x-redwood-fallback`.
Rafael (eng-runtime): I can see the fallback trigger: autoscaler reclaimed a GPU in pool us-west-2:pool-3 during a background maintenance at 1763001188. Canary had increased concurrency, and our routing policy allowed fallback to q4 variant when GPU not available.
Priya (eng-platform): Policy is `allow_fallback=true` by default for non-enterprise tenants. Acme is enterprise but they don't have tenant flag set because onboarding metadata missed a tag. Fix 1: set tenant_acme no-fallback flag immediately. Fix 2: tighten fallback to only use variants with parity (fp16/q8) and avoid q4_0 for prompt-sensitive customers.
Erin (CS): Alex — temporary workaround: we can pin model for your tenant to `redwood-7b-v1.3-fp16` so fallback is disabled. Would you like us to do that now?
Alex (Acme): Yes please. That'll be fine short-term. We need to know root cause and permanent fix.
Rafael (eng-runtime): Action plan: 1) Pin tenant to fp16 variant (hotfix) 2) Roll back routing policy change from canary affecting `us-west-2:pool-3` 3) Add a test that compares semantic outputs across variants for a set of eval prompts (prevent future silent regressions).
Priya (eng-platform): I'm going to push config change to tenant flags now. deploy-bot: deploy started for config-service commit 4f9d2a
deploy-bot: deploy success for config-service at 1763001500
Priya (eng-platform): Tenant flag updated: tenant_acme.allow_fallback=false
Rafael (eng-runtime): After pinning, I see both subsequent requests return x-redwood-variant=fp16 and outputs match. Confirmed on logs:
sre-bot: audit: tenant=tenant_acme action=pin_variant variant=fp16 actor=priya commit=4f9d2a
Rafael (eng-runtime): For permanent fix: propose we change default fallback policy to deny for customers with >$X/mo spend, and to only permit fallbacks to variants that pass a semantic-similarity threshold for a provided eval set. Also add metric `variant_semantic_shift` to alert when >threshold.
Erin (CS): Alex, we'll follow up with a postmortem and proposed policy changes. For now pinned and monitoring. Sorry for the disruption. :lock:
Alex (Acme): Thanks, Erin and team. Appreciate the quick response. Please share the reproducer so our engineers can validate on their side.
Rafael (eng-runtime): Pasted repro script (short):
```python
import requests
for i in range(10):
  r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', json={
    'model':'redwood-7b-v1.3','input':'Summarize how to onboard a user in our app','conversation_id':'conv-9c3'
  }, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer $TOKEN','X-Tenant-Id':'tenant_acme','X-Client-Request-Id':f'repro-{i}'})
  print(i, r.headers.get('x-redwood-variant'), r.headers.get('x-redwood-fallback'))
```
Priya (eng-platform): I'll schedule the rollback/patch for the canary policy and open a ticket to add the semantic parity gate to the routing service. Ticket: PLAT-1729.
Rafael (eng-runtime): I'll own the eval harness (ENG-984). Will add a small set of customer-provided prompts to verify parity across candidate variants.
Erin (CS): Follow-ups: Erin to send postmortem to Alex in 24h, Priya to confirm policy rollback window, Rafael to attach logs and the semantic-similarity metrics.
Erin (CS): Interim note to CS team – if any other customers report inconsistent behavior after rollouts, immediately ask for `x-redwood-variant` response header and `X-Client-Request-Id` and escalate to eng-runtime.
Priya (eng-platform): Also adding alert: route-fallback-rate > 1% for enterprise-tenants -> page oncall.
Rafael (eng-runtime): Logged root cause: routing fallback to q4_0 variant during GPU reclaim causing semantic drift. Remediation: pin tenant, adjust policy, add evals.
Erin (CS): Closing the loop with Alex now. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Alex (Acme): Confirm fixed on our side. We'll reopen if anything else shows up.
